LESSON: A CROSS-REPO FIXTURE IS ONLY A CONTRACT AT THE BLOB LEVEL. The fixture is the P-297 contract between two repos, and the only check that survives a Windows checkout is `git hash-object` (and `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` on the committed object) equalling the upstream blob. A byte-count or a text diff would have passed on a copy that git was about to rewrite into CRLF, and git even warns 'LF will be replaced by CRLF' on that exact file while committing it.

A DIVERGENCE TEST CAN BE VACUOUS, AND THE FIX IS CHEAP: if every row pinned the same answer, 'the rule agrees with every row' would pass for any rule. Assert that the fixture SPANS the decision space (both slate answers, every cell kind, every refusal code, a null form) in the same test file, so an agreement-everywhere equality cannot be mistaken for proof.

A TEST WHOSE EXPECTATION IS DERIVED FROM THE FUNCTION UNDER TEST CANNOT FAIL FOR THE REASON IT EXISTS. Here the fixture is an artefact of the OTHER repo, which is what gives the row-by-row comparison its teeth; the pinned-name list is hand-kept in this repo a second time for the same reason. Both were proven able to fire by editing one side alone.

RE-POINTING A RETIRED ASSERTION IS WHERE A LANE CAN QUIETLY WEAKEN ITS OWN SUITE. Four expectations in this lane's own test file asserted the behaviour the lane removes. Deleting them would have been green, and merely changing the expected strings would have been green too, while losing the P-293 coverage. What worked: keep the untouched half (the verdict vocabulary assertions) exactly as it was, read the new expectations off a fixture the test actually populates, and ADD the fail-closed half of the new ruling on top - then prove with a mutation that all five affected tests still fire.

STOP BEFORE 'FIXING' A LOCAL-ONLY FAILURE. The repo-root test run fails 5 engine-core files on this Windows box while CI is green on the same commit.
